clue.text: Effect of backing motorway agreement

indicators.note: backing tells us to read the motorway's name from the end to the start

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's best-known motorway, written here as MI
a pact is a formal agreement

explanation.surface: A remark about how supporting a road-building deal might play out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns M1 (MI), Britain's main north-south motorway, into IM.
explanation.definitionFit: The impression or result something produces is its effect.

clue.text: Fit in with General Staff sessions

parts.note: meet as an adjective means fit or proper
GS is the abbreviation for General Staff

explanation.surface: An officer slots a few meetings in with the top brass.
explanation.definitionFit: Gatherings of people to discuss business are sessions.

clue.text: A cheat at heart — and a snake

indicators.note: at heart puts the first pieces into the middle of what follows

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
to con is to cheat

explanation.surface: A deceiver is, deep down, a serpent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' puts A CON into the middle of AND A, splitting it AN...DA.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge South American constrictor is a kind of snake.

clue.text: Cutting the sort of coat six-footer needed

parts.note: a trench coat is a belted military-style raincoat
an insect, such as an ant, has six feet

explanation.surface: A tall person needs a particular coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is an insect with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant criticism is incisive, sharp, sharp as a blade.

clue.text: Tooth like the crescent moon?

explanation.surface: A dentist wonders whether a tooth looks like a new moon.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is literal Latin: two points or horns, as a crescent moon has.
explanation.definitionFit: A premolar is a tooth with two cusps, and anything having two horns or points, as the crescent moon does, can be described the same way.

clue.text: Accommodation scheme for tax-saving

explanation.surface: A lodging arrangement doubles as a way to dodge tax.
explanation.walkthrough: Bed-and-breakfasting was selling shares one day and buying them back the next to lock in a capital gains allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: Overnight lodging with a morning meal, and also a share sale and next-day repurchase to cut capital gains liability.

clue.text: How one may come to grief

definitions.text: How one may come to grief

parts.words: How one may come to grief
parts.note: the idiom 'come ... ' meaning to fail is completed by the missing word

explanation.surface: Someone muses on the ways a person can come to grief.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer completes the phrase 'come ___', to fail or fall apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To come apart in failure is idiomatically to come undone, with this word in place of undone.

clue.text: Value of acid test — this is for lung disease

parts.note: pH is the scale value measuring acidity
taken as written, run together

explanation.surface: A chemist reads off a test result and declares it diagnostic of a lung complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for pulmonary tuberculosis, a wasting illness of the lungs.

clue.text: Importunate creditor with key to one's wretched prison quarters

parts.note: a dun is someone persistently demanding payment
G is a musical key

indicators.note: wretched signals the letters are in a sorry, jumbled state

parts.note: the letters of one's, dropping the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A pushy creditor holds the key to a debtor's miserable cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wretched' scrambles ONES into EONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Underground cells in a castle were used to confine prisoners.

clue.text: Go on, win a crown!

explanation.surface: Encouragement to a contender to go out and become king.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second sense as GET A HEAD: crown is slang for head.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper or advance is to go on in life; and getting a crown, slang for the top of the skull, is gaining a head.

clue.text: Dyestuff is a metal

parts.note: tin is a metallic element

explanation.surface: A plain statement that a dye is a kind of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A red crystalline compound used in making dyes such as indigo.

clue.text: Spanish provincial! as member of chapter? Not on!

indicators.note: Not here tells us to strip the word on out of the longer phrase

parts.note: a minor canon is a cleric attached to a cathedral chapter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a cathedral clergyman would never pass as a Spanish country type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on!' looks like an exclamation of disapproval; it means remove ON from MINOR CANON.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhabitant of Menorca, a Spanish island province, is a native of that part of Spain.

clue.text: Useless flute I put in order

indicators.note: putting letters in order means arranging them afresh into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone tidies away a flute they find pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something futile is pointless or ineffective.

clue.text: Hindrance from Ward?

parts.note: the clue word Ward is the word draw spelt backwards

explanation.surface: A complaint that some person called Ward is getting in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Ward is a surname here only on the surface; its letters are DRAW written back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A disadvantage or snag is a hindrance.

clue.text: Metal frame used to extend clothes-line

definitions.text: Metal frame used to extend clothes-line

parts.words: Metal frame used to extend clothes-line
parts.note: the clothes-line is the outline of a dress, held out by a hooped steel petticoat frame

explanation.surface: A gadget for lengthening a washing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes-line' suggests washing hung out; it means the line or silhouette of the clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian hooped petticoat of steel held a skirt out wide.

clue.text: Revelation for seven churches -here

parts.note: the Book of Revelation is addressed to the seven churches of a Roman province named after this continent

explanation.surface: A preacher pointing to where the seven churches of Revelation stood.
explanation.walkthrough: Revelation 1:4 opens 'John to the seven churches which are in' this place; Revelation is the Bible book, not a disclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: The seven churches of the Apocalypse lay in the Roman province of that name in Asia Minor.

clue.text: The Emperor John

explanation.surface: A reference to a particular emperor called John.
explanation.walkthrough: Augustus John was a Welsh portrait painter; Augustus was the first Roman emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavian took this title as first Roman ruler, and it was the first name of the painter Augustus John.

clue.text: Mother is disturbed by temperature on chart

indicators.note: being disturbed means these letters are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: A mother is worried by a fever chart.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'is' gives letters; the second, in 'is disturbed', is part of the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather map, a line joining places of equal temperature.

clue.text: River-goddess's double life

indicators.note: double means the short word for being alive is written twice

parts.note: life is existence, being: what 'is' expresses

explanation.surface: A nymph of the river leads two lives.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isis is the Thames at Oxford and also an Egyptian goddess, so one word covers 'River-goddess'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian deity shares her name with the stretch of the Thames flowing through Oxford.

clue.text: Measure conspirator detailed was incomplete

parts.note: an inch is a unit of length

indicators.note: detailed means the conspirator's name loses its tail, the final letter

parts.note: Titus Oates invented the Popish Plot of 1678

explanation.surface: An account of a plot was measured and found lacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'thorough' but means de-tailed, losing the last letter of OATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchoate means only begun, undeveloped, not complete.

clue.text: Swollen as result of blow

explanation.surface: A bruise puffed up after a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow' suggests a punch; it means blowing air in.
explanation.definitionFit: Puffed up with air, as a balloon is when someone blows into it.

clue.text: Greek Metropolitan produces three articles about six counties

indicators.note: about means the article letters go around the county abbreviation

parts.note: A, THE and AN are the three English articles
Northern Ireland, NI, is made up of six counties

explanation.surface: An Orthodox archbishop issues a grammar lesson and a note on Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: A Metropolitan sounds like a churchman; here it is someone from the metropolis.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Greece's capital city is a native of the metropolis.

clue.text: Current measure gives me a term for revision

indicators.note: something put up for revision is to be reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student says a gauge supplies a word to revise.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument that measures electric current in amperes.

clue.text: I'm left out unusually in the last month

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters should be put in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: Someone complains they were excluded, strangely, only last month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges IM, L and OUT. Ultimo is formal letter-writing style for 'of last month'.
explanation.definitionFit: In old commercial letters 'the 5th ultimo' meant the fifth of the previous month.

clue.text: Evidence of fall-out in wood said to be incomplete

indicators.note: said to be tells us to listen to how the next words sound rather than how they are spelt

parts.note: something incomplete is not whole

explanation.surface: A forester gives a half-told account of radioactive fallout among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall-out' suggests radiation; it is a knot literally falling out of a plank.
explanation.definitionFit: When a knot drops out of timber it leaves a gap in the board.

clue.text: Open port for foreigners by arrangement

explanation.surface: A harbour opened to overseas traders after an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a TREATY port, such as those opened to Western trade in China.
explanation.definitionFit: A port opened to foreign trade by international agreement was a treaty port, and a formal agreement between states is itself one.

clue.text: One cannot drink outside in Spain

indicators.note: outside means the drink goes round the other pieces

parts.note: ale is a drink
one is the Roman numeral I
cannot is can't, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone lamenting they are not allowed to drink outdoors on a Spanish holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The Costa Blanca port city is a place found in Spain.

clue.text: Protector once in the West Country

explanation.surface: A former guardian living in south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Seymour, Duke of Somerset, was Lord Protector for the boy king Edward VI; the West Country is south-west England, where the county of that name lies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke who governed for Edward VI bore this title, and it names a county in south-west England.

clue.text: Alters conclusion in historic telegram

indicators.note: in places the word for an ending inside the telegram's name

parts.note: the Ems telegram of 1870 helped spark the Franco-Prussian War
a conclusion is an end

explanation.surface: Someone rewrites the ending of a famous old telegram.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ems telegram, edited by Bismarck, provoked France into war in 1870.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct or revise a text is to alter it.
